title: The Hollow Oath Anew
premise: Bram Joubert has spent her life in Hollowmere, a valley warded against magic where her beast-speaking gift is a death sentence if discovered. When a dying cartographer named Sef presses a bloodstained map into her hands, she learns the valley is not a sanctuary but a prison built on the erased borders of Vael, a country magically unmade a century ago—and Sef's map is the only guide to its last surviving door. Hunted by the Wardens who enforce Hollowmere's silence, Bram flees with a disgraced Warden deserter, Tam, and a one-eyed crow who is more than a crow, following the map through landscapes where erased memories bleed back into the world. At the door, she must choose: walk through and inherit Vael's throne and its unfinished war, or seal the door forever and let a nation's memory die. Bram chooses a third path—she carries Vael's memory out as a story instead of a crown, breaking the inheritance cycle, and returns to Hollowmere to build a found family that no ward can keep out.
about_author: Quentin Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border towns that no longer appear on maps. They write fantasy about the stubborn persistence of memory, and live somewhere deliberately unlisted.

chapters.title: The Valley That Keeps Its Mouth Shut
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. We meet Bram in Hollowmere, quietly using her forbidden gift to calm a neighbor's dying mare while hiding her ability from everyone, including her adoptive aunt Maren. The chapter establishes the valley's suffocating peace and Bram's loneliness. Emotional beat: the ache of being unseen even by those who love you.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ford
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A half-dead stranger, Sef, collapses near the ford, raving about a door. Bram hides him and, when Wardens sweep the village, he presses a bloodstained map into her hands and dies whispering that she is 'the last speaker of Vael.' Bram is now marked. Emotional beat: terror of inheriting a burden she never asked for.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Burn
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Wardens search Maren's house; Bram flees with the map, and Maren chooses to stay behind and cover for her—revealing she always knew about the gift. At the valley's edge, Bram meets Tam, a Warden deserter who spares her and defects. Emotional beat: grief and the first fragile spark of alliance.

chapters.title: The Map Remembers
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. On the road, the map reveals itself as a living document, redrawing itself as they travel through terrain where erased memories bleed—ghost orchards, a road that hums a lullaby. Tam confesses he once helped burn a village's records. Emotional beat: guilt, and the dawning truth that the map is testing them.

chapters.title: The Crow with One Eye
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A one-eyed crow shadows them, speaking fragments of Vaelish; through her gift, Bram realizes it carries the memories of Vael's last beast-speaker—possibly a relative. The crow leads them to a hidden waystation but also betrays their position to a Warden patrol. Emotional beat: the cost of trusting even family-shaped things.

chapters.title: Ashmarket
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. They shelter in Ashmarket, a border town of exiles and memory-smugglers, where Bram learns others have sought the door and failed. A memory-broker offers Bram a deal: her gift, stripped and sold, in exchange for safe passage. Tam argues for it; Bram refuses. Emotional beat: temptation to stop carrying the past.

chapters.title: The Warden's Hound
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Warden-Captain Ilsa Vey, who has hunted the map for years, catches them; Tam is captured covering Bram's escape. The crow sacrifices an eye's worth of memory to blind the Wardens. Alone, Bram speaks with the land itself for the first time—and it answers in Vaelish. Emotional beat: isolation hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Door in the Unmade Country
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, with Tam freed by the crow's diversion. They cross into the erased interior of Vael, where the map dissolves because they have arrived. The door stands in a field of unburied names. Ilsa Vey arrives, and Bram learns Ilsa is Vaeli herself, sworn to keep the door shut forever. Emotional beat: the enemy's grief mirrors her own.

chapters.title: The Hollow Oath
chapters.summary: Bram and Ilsa's POVs interwoven at the climax. The door demands an oath: inherit Vael and reopen its war, or seal it and forget. Bram refuses both, speaking the names of the dead aloud so the land remembers without a ruler; the oath shatters, and the door opens not into a kingdom but into memory itself. Emotional beat: breaking an inheritance cycle at terrible cost—the crow gives the last of itself.

chapters.title: A Country Told Aloud
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Weeks later, Bram returns to Hollowmere with Tam and Ilsa, who now carries Vael's stories instead of its seal. Maren takes them in; the ward weakens as the valley's purpose dies, and for the first time Bram speaks with beasts openly. She begins telling Vael's story to anyone who will listen. Emotional beat: found family, and a home made of memory rather than walls.
